tools.description: Read structured state for one surface. Desktop returns elements and snapshot_id; detail="compact" controls desktop observation verbosity only. Browser requires tab_id and returns page text/elements. anyOf.description: Backend hint for phone observe and screenshot. scrcpy/none are response states, not request inputs.

tools.description: Capture a fresh desktop frame and return a snapshot_id for pixel actions. Captures exactly one screen, never the whole multi-monitor desktop. With no selector it captures the main display. To drive or verify a specific application, target it instead of relying on the default: pass one window selector (window_id/pid/app_id/wm_class/title) to activate and crop to that window, or one display selector (display_id/display_name/display_index) for a specific monitor. An application on a secondary monitor will not appear in the default main-display capture.

anyOf.description: Exact display_id from environment.displays.
Zero-based display index from environment.displays. Prefer display_id.
Display name/connector from environment.displays. Prefer display_id.

Terminal process ID from desktop window terminal metadata. 0 is ignored.

tools.name: browser_scroll

tools.description: Click, secondary-click, or drag on the desktop. Preferred: pass the snapshot_id from the same capture_desktop/observe plus x/y read off that screenshot; those pixels are translated to the screen for you and work even when no semantic elements are exposed (e.g. Wayland apps with no matched AT-SPI tree). Or pass snapshot_id plus element_index/name/text for a semantic target. Bare x/y with no snapshot_id are raw screen coordinates and should be used only when you have no snapshot. Do not call with only operation.

duration_ms.description: Drag only. Paces the injected pointer path over this many milliseconds of wall-clock time; the drag is always interpolated, but a larger value (~400-800) makes sliders and drag-and-drop gestures track more reliably.

element_identifier.description: Exact backend_ref from a desktop observation; direct semantic target that does not require snapshot_id.

element_index.description: Element index from the same desktop observation; pair with its snapshot_id.

role.description: Optional selector refiner; not a standalone target.

states.description: Optional selector refiners; not a standalone target.

text.description: Snapshot-scoped element text selector; requires snapshot_id.

x.description: Click x coordinate or drag start x. With snapshot_id it is a screenshot pixel from that capture (translated to the screen for you); without snapshot_id it is a raw screen coordinate.

y.description: Click y coordinate or drag start y. With snapshot_id it is a screenshot pixel from that capture (translated to the screen for you); without snapshot_id it is a raw screen coordinate.

tools.description: Click, secondary-click, or drag on the desktop. Preferred: pass the snapshot_id from the same capture_desktop/observe plus x/y read off that screenshot; those pixels are translated to the screen for you and work even when no semantic elements are exposed (e.g. Wayland apps with no matched AT-SPI tree). Or pass snapshot_id plus element_index/name/text for a semantic target. Bare x/y with no snapshot_id are raw screen coordinates and should be used only when you have no snapshot. Do not call with only operation.

duration_ms.description: Drag only. Paces the injected pointer path over this many milliseconds of wall-clock time; the drag is always interpolated, but a larger value (~400-800) makes sliders and drag-and-drop gestures track more reliably.
